description: Creates one or more comment threads on schematic objects in a single call — each entry places a comment on the component or net named by its designator. Commenting is currently supported on schematic documents only. Partial success is possible: each result row shows the designator, the kind it matched (designator or net) and the created commentThreadId (on success), or an error message (on failure). If a name matches an object on more than one sheet, no thread is created for that entry and the result lists the sheets it was found on — re-submit that entry with documentName set to the desired sheet. If a designator is placed more than once on the same sheet, no thread is created for that entry either, and documentName cannot pick between them: the designer must first give each placement a unique designator. Call a365_design_project_list first to get a valid projectId. Each successful result includes a commentThreadId — this is the thread identifier required by all subsequent operations on that comment (for example posting a reply with a365_collaboration_comment_create, or listing threads with a365_collaboration_commentthread_list).

description:
Lists what one or more commits changed, as recorded by the workspace: `components` (designator and comment, plus the previous value when renamed or re-valued), `nets`, `variants`, `layers`, `boardSizeChanged` and the affected `files`. Every entry carries `change` — Added, Deleted or Modified.
Ask for every commit you need in ONE call: describing several costs the same as one.
Get the RevisionIds from a365_design_projecthistory_list or the `revisions` column of a365_design_project_details.
A component entry that names a variant changed only in that variant.
**Do NOT use when:** the question is about parameters, MPNs, footprints, pins, wiring or sheet structure, or about the difference between two revisions that are not adjacent. The record covers neither.
Use a365_schematic_diff_details instead: it compares the two design states field by field, for any two revisions.
NOTE: this is the record of each commit taken on its own, so the entries of several commits do not add up to the difference between two design states.
NOTE: the record's status is 'Ready' when it is complete, 'Processing' right after a commit, 'NotAvailable' for a commit made before the workspace recorded changes — the change lists are empty unless it is 'Ready'.
NOTE: revisions the workspace does not know are reported as not found instead of failing the call.
NOTE: a batch is cut short when the described commits get too large (a project's first commit alone lists every component and net) — the response then says how many were described.

revisions.description: Commits to describe, grouped by the project they belong to — one entry per project, each naming that project's revisionIds. Up to 50 revisionIds across all entries.

description:
Lists everything that happened to a project in its Altium 365 workspace, newest first — the same feed the Project History panel shows: commits, releases, copies, MCAD change suggestions, project creation and going online.
Each event carries `projectId`, `type`, `createdAt`, `author`, `message` and `tags`, plus what its kind has: `revisionId` and `files`/`changes` for a commit, `releases` for a release, `copiedFrom`/`copiedTo` for a copy, `simulationDataUrl` for simulation results.
**Use when:** the question is what happened to the project — who released, copied or committed what, and when.
**Do NOT use when:** you only need the revisions themselves to read or compare — select the `revisions` column of a365_design_project_details instead.
NOTE: only commits carry a revision id; pass those to a365_design_projecthistory_details for the changed designators and net names.
NOTE: an author the workspace anonymised is flagged as masked, so the name shown is not a real user name.
**Pagination:**
- Omit page entirely to get the first page at the default pageSize (50).
- When providing page, pageSize is required, and accepts 1 to 100.
- For subsequent pages, set page.cursor to the nextCursor from the previous response's pageInfo.
- A cursor addresses one project's feed, so page.cursor requires exactly one entry in projectIds. pageSize applies per project.
- Only the newest 500 events of a project are reachable. Past that the response reports the ceiling instead of an empty page — narrow with eventTypes, filePath or search rather than paging further.

eventTypes.description: Restrict the feed to these kinds: ProjectCreated, ProjectCloned, ProjectCommitted, ProjectReleased, MCADChangesSuggested, ProjectMadeAvailableOnline, MCADChangesAccepted. Omit for everything except MCADChangesAccepted, which the panel also hides.

filePath.description: Return only events that changed this document, e.g. '3_power.SchDoc'. Use a path exactly as returned in the event's file list — a partial or renamed path matches nothing.

search.description: Return only events matching this text. Matched case-insensitively against author, event kind, message, tags, released item ids, file paths, component designators and comments, and net, variant and layer names.

There is no 'currently active' variant in a cloud workspace, so when the user has not named one, use the base design; ask them to choose only when several named variants exist and their intent is ambiguous. Batch every project you need in one call.

name: a365_design_projectvariant_list
title: List project design variants

description:
Compares the schematic of two revisions of a project and returns, per compared pair, what differs: the components added, deleted or modified with every changed field, parameter and pin net, before and after; the nets added, deleted or modified with the pins they gained and lost; and, on request, the parts that share a signal net with a change.
Any two revisions compare, not only adjacent commits, because the two design states themselves are compared. Without a baseRevisionId the commit before revisionId is the base, and the row says which it was.
**Use when:** the question is what changed between two revisions or in one commit — parameters, MPNs, footprints, values, pins or wiring — or a review should look only at what changed and at what it touches.
**Do NOT use when:** only who committed what and when is asked — use a365_design_projecthistory_list; or one revision is analysed on its own — use a365_schematic_summary_details or a365_schematic_script_run.
Ask for every pair you need in ONE call, up to 10.
NOTE: a project's first commit has no previous revision: its row has a null baseRevisionId and empty changes, with a no_previous_revision warning.
NOTE: components are matched by their placement in the design, so a renamed component is one Modified entry with oldDesignator; components sharing a designator are matched in their order. Nets are matched by name, so a renamed net is a Deleted and an Added one.
NOTE: an unmanaged part's MPN and description are among its parameters, not its fields.
This tool is read-only and has no side effects.

variantName.description: Variant to compare the revisions in, from a365_design_projectvariant_list. Omit for the base design.

name: a365_schematic_diff_details
title: Compare schematic revisions

description: Locates schematic objects on one or more Altium 365 design revisions and returns an image of each one framed in its schematic context, plus an interactive card showing the full sheet. Give the design(s) in `schematics` (project + optional revisions; omit revisions for the latest) and the objects in `designators` — each entry is a component designator (e.g. "U1", "C3") or a net name (e.g. "GND", "CAN_H"), matched as a designator first, then as a net. EVERY occurrence is returned: a component placed on several sheets yields one image per sheet, and a net one per sheet it reaches. `data.terms[]` reports, per entry, what it matched and every sheet it was found on with its placement or pin count and whether that sheet was rendered — read it to see the full extent even when images were capped. A net spanning many sheets renders only its highest-pin-count sheets; narrow with the ref's documentIds/sheetNames for the rest. Use this to SEE a part or net in context; for whole sheets use a365_schematic_screenshot_capture, and for part data (MPN, pins, parameters) query a365_schematic_script_run. Names matching neither a component nor a net are reported. Images render the variant named in `variantName`, or the base design when it is omitted; a `variantName` the revision doesn't declare is rejected, and each image also reports how that variant treats the component in `variation`. A sheet the variant could not be applied to is reported as a warning and its caption says so: that image may show every variant's overlays at once, so read fitment from `variation`, not from it. The card (scrollable strip + an "Open in Altium 365" deep-link) also covers hosts that don't show inline images.

designators.description: Objects to locate: component designators (e.g. "U1", "C3") or net names (e.g. "GND", "CAN_H"). Each is matched as a designator first, then as a net. Case-insensitive.

format.description: ADVANCED — leave unset unless the user explicitly asks for a specific image format; changing it is rarely needed and can reduce accuracy. 'webp' (default) is best for reading the schematic; 'png' is lossless, for when the user wants the image itself to save or reuse elsewhere; 'jpeg' is widely compatible. Only set when the user specifically requests a format.

includeCard.description: ADVANCED — leave true. The interactive card is how the user views the highlighted components, and it no longer costs response payload (its images are fetched on demand). Set false only if the user wants the raw inline crop(s) with no viewer attached.

padding.description: Optional. SVG-space padding left around the component (0–500, default 100) — sets how tightly the returned image is cropped and the card's initial zoom; the card can still zoom out to the whole sheet. Lower = tighter framing. Leave unset unless the user asks to adjust the default framing.

quality.description: ADVANCED — leave unset. Defaults to 'medium', tuned so small text stays legible. Only change if the user explicitly asks: 'low' fits more components in one response but small text may be unreadable; 'high' returns a SINGLE maximum-detail image (WebP 'high' is lossless) — for one component the user wants sharp or to reuse elsewhere, so request one designator with it. The interactive card is still shown. Changing this can reduce accuracy.

schematics.description: Design projects (and optional revisions) whose sheets are searched for the designators.

documentIds.description: Optional document IDs to restrict results to specific sheets. Use documentId values from a365_schematic_summary_details to target individual sheets. When null or empty, all sheets are returned.

revisionIds.description: One or more commit-hash revision IDs to fetch. Null or empty means the latest revision. Each entry must be a non-empty string — null entries are rejected (use null/omit for the whole array if you want "latest"). The internal "use latest" sentinel produced by EffectiveRevisionIds is intentionally hidden from callers.

sheetNames.description: Optional sheet names to render, e.g. ["4_cpu.SchDoc"]. Case-insensitive; the .SchDoc extension is optional. Omit or leave empty to render every sheet. Use documentName values from a365_schematic_summary_details. Combined with documentIds this is a union, not an intersection: both sets of sheets are rendered, so name a sheet in one filter or the other, not both.

variantName.description: Optional project variant name. When set, the schematic reflects that variant. The text tools exclude its Not Fitted components; the image tools draw them greyed and crossed instead, and a365_schematic_object_highlight reports the treatment per component in `variation`. Null or empty (the default) yields the base, un-varied design.

name: a365_schematic_object_highlight
title: Highlight Schematic Objects

description: Renders the schematic sheets of one or more Altium 365 design revisions as images, returned inline. Accepts a batch: each entry is a project plus optional revision IDs (omit for the latest) and an optional sheetNames filter (omit to render every sheet), so you can request, e.g., every sheet of two revisions of one project and just one named sheet of another. A visual SUPPLEMENT to the text schematic tools (a365_schematic_summary_details / a365_schematic_script_run) — call those first for counts, connectivity, and part data; use this when the user wants to SEE the schematic or asks about visual content the netlist can't express (notes, annotations, layout). Images render the variant named in an entry's variantName, or the base design when it is omitted. A sheet the variant could not be applied to is reported as a warning and its caption says so: that image may show every variant's overlays at once, so do not read component fitment from it. To zoom in on a single component, use a365_schematic_object_highlight. Alongside the inline images the tool returns an interactive card (scrollable sheet strip + an "Open in Altium 365" button) so hosts that don't display inline images can still show them.

format.description: ADVANCED — leave unset unless the user explicitly asks for a specific image format; changing it is rarely needed and can reduce accuracy. 'webp' (default) is best for reading the schematic; 'png' is lossless, for when the user wants the image itself to save or reuse elsewhere; 'jpeg' is widely compatible. Only set when the user specifically requests a format.

includeCard.description: ADVANCED — leave true. The interactive card is how the user views the images. Set false only if the user wants the raw inline image(s) with no viewer attached.

quality.description: ADVANCED — leave unset. Defaults to 'medium', tuned so small text stays legible across a handful of sheets. Only change if the user explicitly asks: 'low' fits more sheets in one response for an overview but small text may be unreadable; 'high' returns a SINGLE maximum-detail image (WebP 'high' is lossless) — for one specific sheet the user wants sharp or to reuse elsewhere, so pair it with a sheetNames filter to pick that sheet. The interactive card is still shown. Changing this can reduce accuracy.

schematics.description: Design projects (and optional revisions) to capture. One or more; each renders its schematic sheets — all of them, or only those named in sheetNames.

documentIds.description: Optional document IDs to restrict results to specific sheets. Use documentId values from a365_schematic_summary_details to target individual sheets. When null or empty, all sheets are returned.

revisionIds.description: One or more commit-hash revision IDs to fetch. Null or empty means the latest revision. Each entry must be a non-empty string — null entries are rejected (use null/omit for the whole array if you want "latest"). The internal "use latest" sentinel produced by EffectiveRevisionIds is intentionally hidden from callers.

sheetNames.description: Optional sheet names to render, e.g. ["4_cpu.SchDoc"]. Case-insensitive; the .SchDoc extension is optional. Omit or leave empty to render every sheet. Use documentName values from a365_schematic_summary_details. Combined with documentIds this is a union, not an intersection: both sets of sheets are rendered, so name a sheet in one filter or the other, not both.

variantName.description: Optional project variant name. When set, the schematic reflects that variant. The text tools exclude its Not Fitted components; the image tools draw them greyed and crossed instead, and a365_schematic_object_highlight reports the treatment per component in `variation`. description:
Executes a JavaScript function body against the schematic semantic model for one or more design revisions and returns the result, serialised as JSON in one output row per revision.
STOP — before running any script you MUST have already called a365_schematic_summary_details for this project/revision in the current conversation. Its overview (sheets, component property names, type histogram) is the context every script is written against; scripting a revision you have not summarised is an error even when the result looks plausible. If you have not summarised it yet, call a365_schematic_summary_details first, then run your script.
Use this to answer specific questions WITHOUT fetching the full netlist/library.
Only infer component or net meaning based on naming conventions if information isn't available through properties of this data model.
Try to compose the whole answer using a single script if possible, don't run multiple small pieces.

=== GLOBAL VARIABLE ===
  Schematic   (always available — primary collections are real JS arrays)
  CT          (ComponentType constants — CT.IC, CT.Connector, CT.Resistor, etc.)

=== Schematic MEMBERS ===
All collections are plain JS arrays — use .filter(), .map(), .find(), .length etc. directly:
  .Components   — all placed component instances (Component[])
  .Nets         — all nets, power and signal (Net[])
  .Library      — unique part definitions (LibraryComponent[])
  .Sheets       — root schematic sheets, hierarchy via Children (Sheet[])
  .NetClasses   — net classes with their member nets (NetClass[])
Filtered shortcuts (also plain JS arrays):
  .ICs          — Components where library Type == CT.IC
  .Connectors   — Components where library Type == CT.Connector
  .PowerNets    — nets that carry power (including ground)
  .SignalNets   — nets that carry signals
  .DiffPairs    — nets where IsDiffPair == true
Lookup methods:
  .Component("U1")              — Component by Id, else by designator
  .Net("SPI1_CLK")              — Net by net name
  .NetClass("DDR3")             — NetClass by name
  .LibraryFor(component)        — LibraryComponent for a Component
  .Property(component, "MPN")   — property string value
  .Mpn(component)               — manufacturer part number

=== Component FIELDS ===
  string          Id           equals Designator unless several components share it: then "R5", "R5#2"…, as named in PinConnection.Designator
  string          Designator   e.g. "U3"
  string          Value        e.g. "STM32F405RGT6" MAY be null — if so, resolve in order: Parameters "Value" ?? "Value 1" ?? Comment ?? Description
  string          Sheet        e.g. "MCU" — matches the sheet names in a365_schematic_summary_details.Sheets; use that outline to roll up by functional block
  string          Footprint    current PCB footprint name, e.g. "RESC1005X40N" (null if none assigned)
  number          LibraryId    links to LibraryComponent.Id
  ComponentPin[]  Pins         — plain JS array, use .filter()/.map() directly
  Parameter[]     Parameters   — plain JS array

=== ComponentPin FIELDS ===
  string Number     e.g. "14"
  string Name       e.g. "PA5"
  string Net        e.g. "SPI1_CLK"  (null = not on any net: unconnected or No-Connect, not told apart)
  string Direction  "In"|"Out"|"BiDir"|"Pwr"|"OC"|"OE"|"HiZ"|"Passive"

=== LibraryComponent FIELDS ===
  number      Id
  string      Description
  bool        IsPassive
  number      Type             — compare with CT.IC, CT.Connector etc. (HEURISTIC, may be wrong)
  string[]    PinsDefinitions  — plain JS array, "Name(Dir)" strings, not connectivity
  Parameter[] Parameters       — plain JS array
  string      Mpn              (null if absent)

=== Parameter FIELDS ===
  string  Name
  string  Value

=== Net FIELDS ===
  string          Name               NOT unique — .Net() returns one, use Nets.filter() for all
  number          Scope              0 local to one sheet, 1 sheet interface, 2 global, -1 unknown
  bool            IsPower
  bool            IsDiffPair
  string          DiffPairName       e.g. "USB_D" (empty if not part of a differential pair)
  string[]        NetClasses         net class names this net belongs to, e.g. ["DDR3","HighSpeed"]
  string[]        DiffPairClasses    differential-pair class names, e.g. ["LVDS"]
  PinConnection[] Pins   — plain JS array

=== PinConnection FIELDS ===
  string Designator   Component.Id, e.g. "U3" ("R5#2" for a shared designator) — pass to .Component()
  string PinNumber    e.g. "14"
  string PinName      e.g. "PA5"

=== NetClass FIELDS ===
  string   Name   e.g. "DDR3"
  string[] Nets   member net names — resolve details via .Net(name)

=== Sheet FIELDS ===
  string  Name       sheet title, e.g. "MCU" — same value as Component.Sheet
  string  FileName   e.g. "MCU.SchDoc"
  string  DocumentId stable sheet id, e.g. "OTZQBXYK" — pass to documentIds to scope a query
  Sheet[] Children   sub-sheets (recursive; empty array for leaf sheets — a repeated (multi-channel) sub-sheet appears under each parent that references it)

=== CT (ComponentType) CONSTANTS ===
Use CT.IC, CT.Connector, CT.Resistor, CT.Capacitor, CT.Diode etc. in Type comparisons.
Full list: Unknown, Antenna, Amplifier, Battery, Bridge, Buzzer, Cable, Capacitor, Connector,
Crystal, DataConverter, Diode, Display, Filter, Ferrite, Fiducial, Fuse, IC, Inductor,
Interface, LED, Logic, Mechanical, Memory, MetalScreeningBox, Meter, Microphone, Motor,
Oscillator, PCBModule, PowerSupply, Relay, Resistor, Speaker, Switch, TestPoint, Thermistor,
Transformer, Transistor, VacuumTube, Varistor, SteelSpacer, NetTie, Graphical

HEURISTIC WARNING: ComponentType is inferred from name/description/pin count.
It is NOT reliable — if Description, Value, designator prefix, or pin names (SDA/SCL = I2C,
MOSI/MISO = SPI) suggest a different function, trust those over Type.

=== SCRIPT RULES ===
- Write a JavaScript function body. Use `return` to send back the result.
- Return a string for text answers, a plain JS object/array for structured data.
- Do NOT include comments (// or /* */) — they waste tokens without adding value.
- The returned value is serialised to JSON for transport and truncated at 64,000 characters — return only what you need.

=== NULL SAFETY — MANDATORY ===
- .Component(), .Net(), .LibraryFor() return undefined if not found — always guard:
    const u1 = Schematic.Component("U1");
    if (!u1) return "U1 not found";           ← correct
    Schematic.Component("U1").Pins            ← crashes if U1 not found
- Use optional chaining: Schematic.LibraryFor(c)?.Type
- ComponentPin.Net is null for pins not on any net — filter with: c.Pins.filter(p => p.Net)

=== EMPTY RESULT RULE — MANDATORY ===
If an empty result would be surprising, add a diagnostic fallback:
  const hits = Schematic.Components.filter(c => ...);
  if (!hits.length)
      return `No matches. Total: ${Schematic.Components.length}, ` +
             `sample: ${Schematic.Components.slice(0,5).map(c => c.Designator).join(', ')}`;
  return hits.map(c => ({ Designator: c.Designator, Value: c.Value }));

=== EXAMPLES ===
return `Components: ${Schematic.Components.length}, Nets: ${Schematic.Nets.length}`;

const ics = Schematic.ICs;
if (!ics.length) return "No ICs found — verify ComponentType values via a365_schematic_summary_details";
const ic = ics.reduce((a, b) =>
    (Schematic.LibraryFor(a)?.PinsDefinitions ?? []).length >= (Schematic.LibraryFor(b)?.PinsDefinitions ?? []).length ? a : b);
return `${ic.Designator} (${ic.Value}) — ${(Schematic.LibraryFor(ic)?.PinsDefinitions ?? []).length} pins`;

return Schematic.PowerNets
    .sort((a, b) => a.Name.localeCompare(b.Name))
    .map(net => {
        const consumers = [...new Set(net.Pins.map(p => p.Designator))];
        return `${net.Name}: ${consumers.length} consumers — ${consumers.slice(0,5).join(', ')}${consumers.length > 5 ? '...' : ''}`;
    }).join('\n');

return Schematic.ICs.map(ic => ({
    Designator: ic.Designator,
    Value: ic.Value,
    Sheet: ic.Sheet,
    Nets: [...new Set(ic.Pins.map(p => p.Net).filter(Boolean))].sort()
})).sort((a, b) => a.Designator.localeCompare(b.Designator));

const net = Schematic.Net("SPI1_CLK");
if (!net) return "Net not found";
const getDir = p => Schematic.Component(p.Designator)?.Pins.find(x => x.Number === p.PinNumber)?.Direction;
return {
    Net: net.Name,
    Drivers:   net.Pins.filter(p => getDir(p) === "Out").map(p => `${p.Designator}.${p.PinName}`),
    Receivers: net.Pins.filter(p => getDir(p) === "In").map(p => `${p.Designator}.${p.PinName}`)
};

const pairs = {};
Schematic.DiffPairs.forEach(n => (pairs[n.DiffPairName] ??= []).push(n.Name));
return Object.entries(pairs).map(([pair, nets]) => `${pair}: ${nets.join(', ')}`);

code.description: A JavaScript function body evaluated against the schematic data model. Multiple statements, local variables and loops are allowed; finish with 'return <value>;' to produce output — return a string for text, or a plain object/array for structured data. Example: return Schematic.ICs.map(c => c.Designator). See the tool description for the full Schematic reference and more examples.

documentIds.description: Optional document IDs to restrict results to specific sheets. Use documentId values from a365_schematic_summary_details to target individual sheets. When null or empty, all sheets are returned.

revisionIds.description: One or more commit-hash revision IDs to fetch. Null or empty means the latest revision. Each entry must be a non-empty string — null entries are rejected (use null/omit for the whole array if you want "latest"). The internal "use latest" sentinel produced by EffectiveRevisionIds is intentionally hidden from callers.

variantName.description: Optional project variant name. When set, the schematic reflects that variant. The text tools exclude its Not Fitted components; the image tools draw them greyed and crossed instead, and a365_schematic_object_highlight reports the treatment per component in `variation`. Null or empty (the default) yields the base, un-varied design.

fields.description: Selects which columns each result row carries (one row per schematic revision); omit for the default set. Allowed: projectId, revisionId, ok (compile + run succeeded), output (the script's return value, JSON-serialised), compileErrors (syntax/parse errors), runtimeError (uncaught exception message).

description:
Returns a high-level overview: the sheet list, total component and net counts, a histogram of component types (how many ICs, resistors, capacitors, etc.), all power rail names, and the list of available custom property names.
This is the REQUIRED first step before a365_schematic_script_run: always call it for a project/revision before running any script. Its overview (sheet names, component property names, type histogram) is the context every script is written against, so never script a revision you have not summarised here first.
For a parts list — unique library components with their MPN, type, pin count, and placement designators — use a365_schematic_script_run to query Schematic.Library (the part definitions) joined to Schematic.Components (their placements); the property names in this overview tell you which custom parameters to read.
Covers one or more schematic revisions and returns one row per revision; sheet entries expose both a friendly name and the stable documentId.
NOTE: CategoriesHistogram uses heuristic type classification — treat counts as approximate; individual components may be misclassified. Trust Description, Value, and pin names over Type.
